classification.difficultyReason: Requires identifying matching triangles within intersecting parallel-line geometry, justifying angle correspondence, and connecting corresponding-side ratios with segment addition to obtain whole-to-part ratios.

spec.description: E, D, A are collinear; E, F, G, B are collinear; D, F, C are collinear; A, G, C are collinear. AB is parallel to DC, and EA is parallel to BC. Matching double and single arrow marks preserve these two parallel families. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: Intersecting transversals within parallel lines; no numerical measurements are supplied in the diagram.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle AGB$ is similar to $\triangle CGF$.

answer.short: $\triangle AGB\sim\triangle CGF$ (AAA): vertically opposite angles at $G$ and alternate angles in parallel lines.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle AGB$ and $\triangle CGF$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle AGB&=\angle CGF &&\text{(vertically opposite angles)},\\\angle GAB&=\angle GCF &&\text{(alternate angles, }AB\parallel FC\text{)}.\end{align*}$$
The third pair of angles is also equal, so $\triangle AGB\sim\triangle CGF$ (AAA), with $A\leftrightarrow C$, $G\leftrightarrow G$ and $B\leftrightarrow F$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Name two triangles similar to $\triangle EFD$.

answer.worked:
$\triangle EFD\sim\triangle EBA$ (AAA): the angle at $E$ is common, and corresponding angles are equal because $FD\parallel BA$.

$\triangle EFD\sim\triangle BFC$ (AAA): the angles at $F$ are vertically opposite, and alternate angles are equal because $ED\parallel BC$.

Thus the two triangles, in matching vertex order, are $\triangle EBA$ and $\triangle BFC$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Given that $DF:FC=2:1$, and using your answers to parts a and b, find:

answer.worked:
From $\triangle EFD\sim\triangle BFC$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{EF}{BF}&=\frac{DF}{FC}\\\frac{EF}{BF}&=2.\end{align*}$$
Hence $EF:FB=2:1$, so $EB:EF=3:2$.

From $\triangle EFD\sim\triangle EBA$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AB}{DF}&=\frac{EB}{EF}\\\frac{AB}{DF}&=\frac{3}{2}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $AB:DF=3:2$.

From $\triangle EFD\sim\triangle BFC$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{EF}{FB}&=\frac{DF}{FC}\\\frac{EF}{FB}&=2.\end{align*}$$
Let $FB=k$. Then $EF=2k$ and $EB=EF+FB=3k$.

Thus $EF:EB=2:3$.
